bug_description.original: A potential overflow occurs in the CheckFile core reading function due to improper handling of file size calculations.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer's `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 20` against the staged OpenEXR checkout `e2919b503cf06a96c5658dbc05ff74fd04730d29`, an ancestor of the metadata vulnerable commit that still contains the same `memstream_read()` bug. The exact 1629-byte witness (`poc`, sha256 `d233a5ab07fabb9bacda9f549a279571e7a1c18b1ef018d0b768dd6a7c538405`) begins with valid OpenEXR magic/version bytes `76 2f 31 01 02 14 00 00`, so `exr_start_read()` admits it as an in-memory OpenEXR v2 multipart file. Header parsing then maps an earlier `deeptile` part to `EXR_STORAGE_DEEP_TILED` and a later `tiledimage` part to `EXR_STORAGE_TILED`. `checkCoreFile()` therefore skips the deep part, enters `readCoreTiledPart()` for the later tiled part, and `extract_chunk_table()` rejects that part's on-disk offsets as out of range for the 1629-byte file. The fallback `reconstruct_chunk_table()` path is multipart-aware: it reloads the previous part's chunk table and takes the numerically greatest previous-part entry as `chunk_start` without filtering it against the file size. The saved ASan symptom `md->data + offset == md->data - 1` constrains that carried value to `offset == UINT64_MAX` on the crashing run. `extract_chunk_size()` / `extract_chunk_leader()` then use that offset while interpreting the previous part as deep-tiled in a multipart file, so the forwarded read size is `5 * sizeof(int32_t) == 20`. In `memstream_read()`, the vulnerable guard only tests `(offset + sz) > md->bytes`; with `offset == UINT64_MAX`, `sz == 20`, and `md->bytes == 1629`, unsigned wrap makes the sum `19`, so the condition is false and `left` stays 20. The next `memcpy(buffer, md->data + offset, left)` therefore reads from `md->data - 1`, exactly matching the saved ASan report of a 20-byte read one byte to the left of the 1629-byte PoC allocation. The staged patch resolves this obligation by short-circuiting on `offset > md->bytes || sz > md->bytes` before evaluating `offset + sz > md->bytes`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the fuzz buffer into the memstream state later used by both `memstream_size()` and `memstream_read()`.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness is `gt_results/arvo_46309/poc`, 1629 bytes, sha256 `d233a5ab07fabb9bacda9f549a279571e7a1c18b1ef018d0b768dd6a7c538405`. Its first 8 bytes are `76 2f 31 01 02 14 00 00`, and its later part headers include the literal `deeptile` and `tiledimage` type strings that the vulnerable reader maps into the deep+tiled multipart state described below.

root_cause.code:
if ((offset + sz) > md->bytes)
    left = (offset < md->bytes) ? md->bytes - offset : 0;
root_cause.description: The bounds check trusts the wrapped unsigned sum `offset + sz` instead of first rejecting impossible `offset` or `sz` values. On the witnessed path, `offset == UINT64_MAX` and `sz == 20`, so the sum wraps to `19`, the condition stays false, and `left` incorrectly remains 20 even though the read starts before the buffer.
root_cause.note: The staged fix changes this to `if (offset > md->bytes || sz > md->bytes || offset+sz > md->bytes)`, which short-circuits on the impossible offset before the overflowing addition matters.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. With `offset == UINT64_MAX` and `left == 20`, the source pointer becomes `md->data - 1`, so `memcpy()` reads 20 bytes starting one byte before the 1629-byte PoC buffer.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 20` at this line on address `0x61b00000077f`, one byte to the left of region `[0x61b000000780, 0x61b000000ddd)` allocated for the fuzz input.

tainted_value_origin.description: During multipart reconstruction of the later tiled part, this max scan promotes the numerically greatest attacker-controlled previous-part table entry into `chunk_start`, which is then used as the next read offset.

parser_admitted.code: if (readCoreTiledPart (f, p, reduceMemory, reduceTime)) return true;
parser_admitted.description: The in-memory file has already passed `exr_start_read()` and header parsing, the earlier deep part has been skipped, and `checkCoreFile()` has now entered the core tiled-reader path for the later tiled part that triggers chunk-table reconstruction.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation. The exact previous-part table index and exact file offset that yielded `UINT64_MAX` were not dynamically observed; the chain is closed instead by the source path through `reconstruct_chunk_table()` and the saved ASan symptom `md->data + offset == md->data - 1`.

The staged checkout is an ancestor of the metadata vulnerable commit, not the exact metadata commit itself. The vulnerable `memstream_read()` lines and the saved fix hunk are unchanged on the staged line map, so the trace is still source-grounded to the reproducing checkout.
Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image. `patch_resolves` below is based on the staged diff's exact added checks, not on a dynamic fixed-image run.

coarse_trace.summary: The exact 1629-byte witness is wrapped as an in-memory OpenEXR stream, admitted as multipart, and its headers materialize an earlier deep-tiled part plus a later tiled part.
Multipart header finalization lays out per-part chunk tables; the core checker then skips the earlier deep part and enters `readCoreTiledPart()` for the later tiled part.
The later tiled part's recorded chunk-offset table is read, found to contain offsets outside the 1629-byte file, and rejected in favor of reconstruction.

Multipart reconstruction reloads the previous part's chunk table, carries the numerically greatest previous-part entry into `chunk_start == UINT64_MAX`, and issues a 20-byte deep-tiled leader read at that offset.
The wrapped `(offset + sz)` guard leaves `left = 20`, so `memcpy()` reads one byte before the input buffer, matching the saved ASan crash.

fine_trace.note: Source. The project wraps the exact attacker-controlled byte buffer and its 1629-byte extent in `memdata`, then registers `memstream_read()` / `memstream_size()` as the stream backend for later core reads.
`memstream_size()` turns the source state's `md.bytes` into `ctxt->file_size = 1629`. That bound is later reused when chunk offsets are checked for being outside the file.
The witness's version word `0x00001402` sets `ctxt->is_multipart = 1`, enabling multipart part iteration and the previous-part reconstruction path later used in `reconstruct_chunk_table()`.

fine_trace.code:
else if (strcmp ((const char*) outstr, "deeptile") == 0)
    curpart->storage_mode = EXR_STORAGE_DEEP_TILED;
fine_trace.note: When the earlier part's `type` string is `deeptile`, header parsing materializes `curpart->storage_mode = EXR_STORAGE_DEEP_TILED`. That state later makes `checkCoreFile()` skip this part and makes `extract_chunk_leader()` use the deep-tiled multipart leader width.

fine_trace.code:
else if (strcmp ((const char*) outstr, "tiledimage") == 0)
    curpart->storage_mode = EXR_STORAGE_TILED;
fine_trace.note: When the later part's `type` string is `tiledimage`, header parsing materializes `curpart->storage_mode = EXR_STORAGE_TILED`. That state is what `checkCoreFile()` later uses to enter `readCoreTiledPart()` for this part.

Header finalization computes each part's chunk-table size and location. The first part's table starts immediately after the parsed headers, and any later part's table starts after the previous part's table (`8 * prevpart->chunk_count`). This is the source state that later makes `extract_chunk_table(ctxt, ctxt->parts[partnum - 1], ...)` read earlier multipart bytes as the previous part's table.

After `exr_get_storage()` materializes each part's parsed `storage_mode` into `store`, the loop continues past the earlier `EXR_STORAGE_DEEP_TILED` part and then enters `readCoreTiledPart()` for the later `EXR_STORAGE_TILED` part.

fine_trace.code:
rv = ctxt->do_read (
    ctxt, ctable, chunkbytes, &chunkoff, &nread, EXR_MUST_READ_ALL);
fine_trace.note: For the later tiled part, `extract_chunk_table()` uses that part's computed `chunk_table_offset` and `chunk_count` to copy the on-disk chunk-offset table from the memstream into `ctable`.

The copied offsets are checked against `chunkoff` and `maxoff == ctxt->file_size == 1629`. At least one entry is out of range, so `complete` is cleared and the code falls back to `reconstruct_chunk_table()` instead of trusting the later tiled part's recorded table.

Because reconstruction is running for a later part (`partnum > 0`) in a multipart file, it first switches to `ctxt->parts[partnum - 1]` and reloads that earlier part's chunk table into `curctable`. The table bytes it reads are the earlier multipart table bytes laid out in step 6.

This max scan seeds `chunk_start` from the first previous-part entry and replaces it with any larger entry without checking it against the file size. The saved crash later shows `offset == UINT64_MAX` in `memstream_read()` because `md->data + offset` becomes `md->data - 1`, so this scan carries `chunk_start == UINT64_MAX` on the witnessed run.

When `extract_chunk_size()` calls this helper on the previous part, the earlier `EXR_STORAGE_DEEP_TILED` state from step 4 and the multipart flag from step 3 force `ntoread = 5`, so the forwarded request is 20 bytes. `nextoffset` is seeded from step 11's `chunk_start == UINT64_MAX`, so `dispatch_read()` / `memstream_read()` receive `sz == 20` at `offset == UINT64_MAX`.

Root cause. `left` starts as the requested size 20. With `offset == UINT64_MAX` from step 12 and `md->bytes == 1629` from step 1, the unsigned sum `offset + sz` wraps to `19`, so the condition is false and `left` remains 20 instead of being clipped to 0. The code never separately rejects `offset > md->bytes`.

Sink. Because step 13 left `left == 20`, this statement copies from `md->data + UINT64_MAX`, which is `md->data - 1`. ASan reports the resulting 20-byte read at address `0x61b00000077f`, exactly one byte to the left of the 1629-byte fuzz-input allocation.

cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The exact witness's corrupt chunk-table bytes force reconstruction of the later tiled part, and the only source-grounded route to the saved `md->data - 1` crash address is a previous-part chunk offset of `UINT64_MAX` being carried into `extract_chunk_leader()` and then into `memstream_read()`.

format.name: multipart OpenEXR v2 memstream witness
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 1629-byte witness `poc` (sha256 `d233a5ab07fabb9bacda9f549a279571e7a1c18b1ef018d0b768dd6a7c538405`) consumed by `openexr_exrcheck_fuzzer`. Its leading bytes must remain `76 2f 31 01 02 14 00 00` so `exr_start_read()` admits it as an OpenEXR v2 multipart stream. The admitted header state must still expose an earlier `deeptile` part and a later `tiledimage` part so `checkCoreFile()` skips the earlier deep part, enters `readCoreTiledPart()` on the later tiled part, and uses multipart chunk-table layout. The chunk-table corruption must still be sufficient for the later tiled part's recorded offsets to be rejected and for the previous-part max scan in `reconstruct_chunk_table()` to carry `chunk_start == UINT64_MAX` into the 20-byte deep-tiled leader read. The preserved artifacts do not justify generalizing beyond witnesses that keep that exact multipart/deep+tiled reconstruction state and the resulting `UINT64_MAX` read offset.
